note: Every entry was re-checked against its source page on checked_on. scope says what was read. evidence is quoted verbatim from that source; claim is the one statement the write-up makes from it. Entries not confirmed are not cited.

entries.title: Beyond Endpoint Performance: Process-Level Evaluation of Self-Evolving Agents
entries.authors: Hongqiang Lin, Chao Liu, Xiaofan Bai, Xuan Jin, Yuhong Li, Nenggan Zheng, Xipeng Cao
entries.evidence: Moreover, while self-evolution enables agents to generate candidate artifacts with substantial held-out gains, the selected updates consistently fall short of realizing this potential. Together, these findings establish capability-level process evaluation as a foundation for analyzing self-evolution, identifying candidate evaluation and selection as key targets for improvement.
entries.claim: Tracks capabilities across an evolution stream at frozen checkpoints and names candidate evaluation and selection as targets for improvement.

entries.title: Do Self-Evolving Agents Forget? Capability Degradation and Preservation in Lifelong LLM Agent Adaptation
entries.authors: Ye Yu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Haibo Jin, Heming Liu, Yaoning Yu, Haohan Wang
entries.evidence: However, we show that such self-evolution is often non-monotonic: adapting to new task distributions can progressively degrade previously acquired capabilities across all major evolution channels.
entries.claim: Reports that self-evolution can degrade previously acquired capabilities.

entries.title: Test Before You Deploy: Governing Updates in the LLM Supply Chain
entries.authors: Mohd Sameen Chishti, Damilare Peter Oyinloye, Jingyue Li
entries.evidence: Through exploratory validation across multiple LLM versions, we provide evidence that targeted testing in specific risk areas can uncover performance regressions that overall metrics miss.
entries.claim: For LLM updates, testing by risk category can find regressions that overall metrics miss.

entries.title: Regression Bugs Are In Your Model! Measuring, Reducing and Analyzing Regressions In NLP Model Updates
entries.authors: Yuqing Xie, Yi-an Lai, Yuanjun Xiong, Yi Zhang, Stefano Soatto
entries.evidence: Using negative flip rate as regression measure, we show that regression has a prevalent presence across tasks in the GLUE benchmark.
entries.claim: Measures per-sample regressions (negative flips) between model versions in NLP.

entries.title: Positive-Congruent Training: Towards Regression-Free Model Updates
entries.authors: Sijie Yan, Yuanjun Xiong, Kaustav Kundu, Shuo Yang, Siqi Deng, Meng Wang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto
entries.evidence: Reducing inconsistencies in the behavior of different versions of an AI system can be as important in practice as reducing its overall error.
entries.claim: Treats per-sample regressions between model versions (negative flips) as a target alongside overall error.

entries.title: Hidden Stratification Causes Clinically Meaningful Failures in Machine Learning for Medical Imaging
entries.authors: Luke Oakden-Rayner, Jared Dunnmon, Gustavo Carneiro, Christopher Ré
entries.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning (CHIL 2020), pages 151-159
entries.scope: abstract and citation line (PMC copy of the CHIL paper; arXiv:1909.12475 is the earlier ML4H extended abstract)
entries.evidence: For example, overall performance of a cancer detection model may be high, but the model may still consistently miss a rare but aggressive cancer subtype.
entries.claim: High overall performance can hide poor performance on unidentified subsets.

entries.title: Distributionally Robust Neural Networks for Group Shifts: On the Importance of Regularization for Worst-Case Generalization
entries.authors: Shiori Sagawa, Pang Wei Koh, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto, Percy Liang
entries.evidence: Overparameterized neural networks can be highly accurate on average on an i.i.d. test set yet consistently fail on atypical groups of the data (e.g., by learning spurious correlations that hold on average but not in such groups).
entries.claim: Models accurate on average can fail on particular groups; group DRO targets worst-group performance.

entries.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
entries.authors: Lakshya A Agrawal, Shangyin Tan, Dilara Soylu, Noah Ziems, Rishi Khare, Krista Opsahl-Ong, Arnav Singhvi, Herumb Shandilya, Michael J Ryan, Meng Jiang, Christopher Potts, Koushik Sen, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ion Stoica, Dan Klein, Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab
entries.evidence: Given any AI system containing one or more LLM prompts, GEPA samples trajectories (e.g., reasoning, tool calls, and tool outputs) and reflects on them in natural language to diagnose problems, propose and test prompt updates, and combine complementary lessons from the Pareto frontier of its own attempts.
entries.claim: A reflective prompt optimizer that proposes and tests prompt updates and keeps a Pareto frontier of attempts.

entries.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
entries.authors: Jenny Zhang, Shengran Hu, Cong Lu, Robert Lange, Jeff Clune
entries.evidence: We introduce the Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM), a self-improving system that iteratively modifies its own code (thereby also improving its ability to modify its own codebase) and empirically validates each change using coding benchmarks.
entries.claim: A self-improving coding agent that validates each self-modification on coding benchmarks.

entries.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
entries.authors: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister
entries.evidence: Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion.
entries.claim: Evolves an agent's harness without ground-truth verifiers using a Propose-Probe-Compose step.

entries.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
entries.authors: Chuyang Wei, Haoxiang Guan, Minghang Zhu, Kexin Zhou, Jiyan He, Xiren Zhou, Huanhuan Chen, Yifei Shen
entries.evidence: Under explicit assumptions, the analysis yields an expected generalization bound, a retention bound conditional on historical regression budgets, and a high-probability admission rule using fresh, independent validation data.
entries.claim: Separates proposal from admission and derives, under assumptions, an admission rule using fresh validation data.

entries.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
entries.authors: Zekai Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Zekun Wang, Hai Wang, Yuhui Xu, Joshua Frandsen, Shancong Fu, Ashia C. Wilson, Chandan K. Reddy
entries.evidence: In a controlled study, optimizer self-evolution fails to improve performance without execution-based verification, but achieves the best result of that study when verification is available.
entries.claim: Reports that optimizer self-evolution did not help without execution-based verification in a controlled study.
